title: School-Core: Functional, Complete, and Multi-Repo Issue-to-PR

questions.prompt: How should the goal treat repositories?
questions.description: School-core receives or selects an issue from a configured repo, clones that repo for the task, runs the student/review pipeline, and proposes a PR back to that repo. Repositories are task targets, not courses or organizations.
questions.recommendedAnswer: One school-core system can be configured for multiple repositories. Each task uses a clone/workspace of its selected repository and the resulting PR targets that same repository. Prove the complete loop on one repo, then verify another repo can be added through configuration without a code fork.

questions.prompt: What should hosted/cloud readiness mean for this goal?
questions.description: Keep the deployment provider undecided unless you have a required target.
questions.recommendedAnswer: A provider-neutral, deployable hosted service with authenticated operator/teacher access, durable state and restore, monitoring, resource limits, and documented recovery; a controlled pilot is enough, not a public SaaS launch or numeric uptime SLA.

questions.prompt: Which documented learning-loop enhancements count as required for ‘complete’?
questions.description: Recommendation: include the named backlog below and defer newly discovered work unless you approve it.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Include the documented gaps: archival memory write/consolidation; learning-aware routing; student tool/skill-use telemetry; asynchronous teacher review with dead-letter handling; per-skill scoring; and board/history retention. Also require student feedback, grounded scoring, and memory to work end to end.

options.label: Async teacher review and dead-letter recovery

questions.prompt: What execution boundary should the goal require for student code?
questions.description: Carry forward your prior decisions: no host fallback, trusted checks separate from repository-provided checks, and the coding agent itself inside the isolated environment.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Every student coding task runs in a disposable VM-backed environment with the agent, repository clone, and shell inside it; model access is mediated without exposing raw host credentials; failures fail closed; a separate trusted verifier checks the exact candidate.

options.label: Prove threat model, then choose substrate
